info.title: Unikraft Cloud Build API
info.description:
This specification describes the Unikraft Cloud build API, served by
blacksmith. A build takes its files from git repositories, https tarballs
or the client's own buildkit session, builds a Unikraft image from a
Kraftfile, or from a Dockerfile alone, on a buildkitd running in the
caller's own account, and pushes the image to registries or imports it into
volumes.

Every request carries the caller's Unikraft Cloud token as a bearer token.
The token is validated against the platform on every request, and the answer
is the caller's identity: everything is scoped to that tenant, and the build
of another tenant is a `404`. Images are pulled and pushed with the caller's
token, unless `registries` gives other credentials for a registry.

Every operation answers a failed request with an HTTP status code and an
`ErrorBody`, which names the failure in `error.code` and explains it in
`error.message`. The status codes an operation can answer with are
documented on the operation. The success responses are plain JSON objects,
except for the progress stream of a build, which is newline-delimited JSON
or plain text.

A part of a request marked as not supported yet is answered with `400` and
the code `unsupported`.

One endpoint is not an HTTP operation and so does not appear below:
`POST /v1/builds/{id}/session` attaches the client's buildkit session to a
waiting build, as an h2c upgrade in the shape of dockerd's `/session`, with
its `X-Docker-Expose-Session-*` headers. After the `101`, the connection
serves the build's session sources, secrets, SSH agents and registry
credentials until the build ends. A session that does not advertise a
method the build needs is answered with `400`, and a build that does not
wait for a session, already has one, or that another user started, with
`409`. A build that no session attaches to within a minute fails. The build
reads from the session only when it needs to, thus a session that ends
early does not end the build, but fails the next read that needs it.

tags.name: builds
tags.description:
A build turns its sources into a Unikraft image, on a buildkitd running
in the caller's own account, and pushes the image to registries or
imports it into volumes. A build runs whether or not anyone is watching
it, and its progress can be followed, replayed from the start, until it
has finished.

post.description:
Create a build. It runs on a builder of the caller's tenant, which is
created on first use, whether or not anyone is watching it, and waits for
a build slot while each of the tenant's builders already runs as many
builds at once as the service allows. A request that uses a part of the full build API this
service does not support yet is answered with `400` and the code
`unsupported`. A tenant that already has as many builds running or waiting
as it may is answered with `429` and the code `too_many_builds`. A
request whose `hints.dedupe` names a running or succeeded build with the
same `output` is answered with `200` and that build, and starts nothing.
With other `output`, the new build pushes the image of a succeeded build.

200.description:
The response message for creating a build whose `hints.dedupe` names an
existing build with the same `output`: `200`, with that build as it is, and
a `Location` header naming it.

Location.description: The path of the existing build, e.g. `/v1/builds/{id}`.

201.description:
The response message for creating a build: `201`, with the new build, which
is `waiting` if it reads anything from the client's session and `running`
otherwise, and a `Location` header naming it.

Location.description: The path of the new build, e.g. `/v1/builds/{id}`.

get.description: List the builds of the caller's tenant, newest first.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only the builds in this state.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description:
The maximum number of builds to return. When omitted, every matching
build is returned.

get.description: Get a build by ID: its state, and its result or error once it has finished.

delete.description:
Delete a finished build by ID: its record and its progress stream. The
images it pushed and the volumes it imported into are left alone. A build
that is still waiting or running is answered with `409`; cancel it first.

204.description: There is no content to send for this request, but the headers may be useful.

post.description:
Cancel a build by ID. A waiting or running build is answered with `202`
and becomes `cancelled` once buildkit has unwound, with its progress stream
ending in an `error` whose code is `cancelled`. A build that has already
finished is left as it is and answered with `200`.

202.description:
The response message for cancelling a build that was still waiting or
running: `202`, with the build as it was; it becomes `cancelled` once
buildkit has unwound.

get.description:
Follow the progress of a build by ID. Every request replays the stream
from the start and ends once the build has finished, with a `result` or an
`error` as its last line, so reconnecting is just asking again.
`Accept: text/plain` renders the stream as text instead of
newline-delimited JSON.

200.description:
The progress stream of a build as newline-delimited JSON: one `BuildEvent`
per line. This is the default rendering, and the one that
`Accept: application/x-ndjson` selects.

builder.description: The name of the builder the build runs on.

kraftfile.description:
The Kraftfile of the request. Absent for a build without one, and for a
build from before the service kept its requests.

contexts.description:
The contexts of the request, where the build gets its files from. Absent
for a build from before the service kept its requests.

platforms.description: The platforms of the request. Absent when the request names none.

build_args.description: The build args of the request, by name. Absent when it has none.

target.description: The Dockerfile stage of the request. Absent when it names none.

no_cache.description: Whether the request ignores the builder's cache.

secrets.description:
The IDs of the secrets of the request, sorted. The service does not keep
their values. Absent when the request has none.

registries.description:
The registry hosts of the request, sorted. The service does not keep
their credentials. Absent when the request has none.

session.description:
The path to attach the build's session at. Only present while the build is
`waiting` for it.

created_at.description: The time the build was created.

started_at.description: The time the build started on its builder. Absent until it has.

finished_at.description: The time the build reached a final state. Absent until it has.

result.description: What the build produced. Only present on a `succeeded` build.

error.description:
Why the build did not succeed. Only present on a `failed` or `cancelled`
build.

Build.description:
A build. `result` and `error` are exclusive: a build that succeeded has the
one, a build that failed or was cancelled has the other, and a build that is
still waiting or running has neither.

context.description:
The build context: the directory the Dockerfile is built in, and the
directory relative paths in the Kraftfile resolve in.

dockerfile.description:
The directory holding the Dockerfile of the rootfs. Defaults to
`context`. The Dockerfile in it is its `filename`, which defaults to the
name of the Dockerfile the Kraftfile builds its rootfs with. Only valid
when the rootfs is built from a Dockerfile.

BuildContexts.description:
The contexts a build is built from, by the names of buildkit's Dockerfile
frontend. Any other key is a named context, for `FROM <name>` and
`COPY --from=<name>`, like `docker buildx build --build-context`, for every
Dockerfile the build runs. Named contexts are only valid when the rootfs or
a rom is built from a Dockerfile.

vertexes.description: The vertices that started or completed.

result.description: What the build produced. Only on the last line, of a succeeded build.

error.description:
Why the build did not succeed. Only on the last line, of a failed or
cancelled build.

BuildEvent.description:
One line of the progress stream of a build. Every line is a buildkit
`SolveStatus` in the shape of `docker buildx build --progress=rawjson`, so
anything that renders buildkit progress renders this stream as-is. Steps
that buildkit does not run itself, such as pulling the kernel, packing the
image and pushing it, are reported as vertices of their own. The last line
of the stream is always exactly one of `result` or `error`, and no other
line carries either.

cache.description:
A name for what the build builds, such as a repository or a project.
The service tries to run builds with the same name on the same builder,
so that they share its cache. Empty or absent means the URL of
`contexts.context` without its query, followed by its `subdir`, and no
name for a session context. Only builds on `default` use it.

dedupe.description:
A key that the caller computes from the files that the build reads from
its sources, for example a hash of the contexts and of a Kraftfile from a
source. The service makes the key of the build from it, from the rest of
the request except `output`, `builder`, `hints.cache`, `no_cache`,
`registries` and the values of `secrets`, and from the version of the
service's image builder. When a build of the caller's tenant with the
same key and `output` is `running` or `succeeded`, the request is answered
with that build and `200`, and no new build starts. Else, when a build
with the same key `succeeded`, the new build pushes its image, or imports
its filesystem, to the new `output`, and builds the image only if it
cannot read it. A request with `no_cache` always starts a new build. Failed builds do not count, and
neither do cancelled builds, from the cancel on. A build that reads from
the client's session is never shared: its request always starts a new
build.

BuildHints.description:
Hints on how to handle a build request. They do not change what the build
builds.

image.description:
The reference to push the built image to, including the tag. The caller
picks the tag, and checks whether it already exists. The push is done with
the caller's token, unless `registries` has credentials for its registry.

volume.description:
The name or UUID of an existing volume to import the built filesystem
into, as cpio, through a short-lived instance in the metro of the volume
that runs with the caller's token. A volume that does not exist is not
created. Only valid for a build without a `kraftfile`, of a single
platform.

metro.description:
The name of the metro of `volume`, only needed when it is not the metro
of the service. Only valid with `volume`.

BuildOutput.description:
Where the result of a build goes: exactly one of an image, named by `image`,
or a volume, named by `volume`.

images.description: The pushed images, one per `image` entry of `output`.

volumes.description: The imported volumes, one per `volume` entry of `output`.

ref.description: The reference the image was pushed to, as requested in `output`.

digest.description: The digest of the pushed image.

platforms.description: The platforms the image was built for, e.g. `kraftcloud/x86_64`.

BuildResultVolume.description: A volume a build imported its filesystem into.

BuildStatus.description:
The state of a build. A build starts as `waiting` or `running` and ends as
`succeeded`, `failed` or `cancelled`; it never leaves a final state.

| State       | Description |
|-------------|-------------|
| `waiting`   | The build waits for a client to attach its buildkit session, and then becomes `running`. |
| `running`   | The build waits for a build slot or for its builder, or is being built. |
| `succeeded` | The build finished and every output was pushed or imported; see `result`. |
| `failed`    | The build failed; see `error`. |
| `cancelled` | The build was cancelled before it finished; `error` says so. |

name.description: The name of the builder. Empty means `default`.

image.description:
The buildkit image the builder boots. Defaults to the service's. An
existing builder matches it by repository, and by registry, tag or digest
when both name one.

memory_mb.description: The memory of the builder, in MiB.

cache_mb.description: The size of the builder's cache volume, in MiB.

autokill.description: Delete the builder once it has been idle for a while, set when it is created.

Builder.description:
The builder a build runs on: a buildkitd instance and its cache volume in the
caller's account. Builds on the same builder share its cache. A builder that
does not exist yet is created from these fields; for one that does, every
field but `name` and `autokill` only has to match it, and one that conflicts
is a `409`.

time_ms.description:
Delete the builder and its cache once it has scaled to zero for this many
milliseconds, past the cooldown that follows its last build. `0` never
does. Without it, `default` is deleted after 7 days and a named builder
never is. A delete lock on the builder's instance keeps it.

BuilderAutokill.description: When to delete an idle builder.

kraftfile.description:
The Kraftfile to build. Without one, the build is the kernel-less image
of `contexts.context` built with the file `Dockerfile`, or with the one
that `contexts.dockerfile` gives, for x86_64 unless `platforms` names
others.

platforms.description:
The platforms to build for. Only the architecture selects, so `x86_64` is
`linux/amd64`. Defaults to the targets of the Kraftfile, or to `x86_64`
when it has none.

build_args.description: The values of the Dockerfile's `ARG`s, by name.

target.description: The Dockerfile stage to build. Defaults to the last one.

builder.description:
The builder to run on. Defaults to `default`, which runs each build on
one of `default`, `default-2`, ..., as many as the service allows: the
first with a free slot, in the order that `hints.cache` gives.

hints.description:
Hints on how to handle the request: where to run the build, and which
existing build to answer instead.

secrets.description: The secrets the build can mount, by ID.

ssh.description: The SSH agents the build can mount, by ID.

registries.description:
The credentials for registries, by host, with `*` for any other host.
`docker.io` names Docker Hub. The caller's token is the credential for
a registry that has none, and so is only used when there is no `*`.

output.description:
Where the result goes. At least one output is required. The outputs are
pushed or imported one after the other, so a build that fails or is
cancelled can leave the first outputs pushed or imported.

CreateBuildRequest.description: The request message for creating a build.

code.description: The code of the error, for a program to act on.

message.description: The reason for the error, for a person to read.

Error.description: Why a request, or a build, failed.

ErrorBody.description:
The response message for a failed request. The HTTP status code says that
the request failed and `error` says why.

ErrorCode.description:
The reason a request, or a build, failed.

The first eight codes are answered by the API together with the HTTP status
code given. The last four are the `code` of the `error` of a build whose
`status` is `failed` or `cancelled`, both in the build itself and in the last
event of its progress stream.

| Code               | Description |
|--------------------|-------------|
| `invalid`          | `400`: the request is malformed, or a value in it is not valid: the body is not JSON, a required field is missing, a source has more than one of `session`, `git` and `url`, an image reference does not parse, a volume output has a `kraftfile` or more than one platform, an inline Kraftfile does not parse or cannot be built, a session does not advertise a method the build needs, ... |
| `unsupported`      | `400`: the request uses a part of the full build API, or of the Kraftfile, that this service does not support yet. Nothing is ignored silently. |
| `unauthenticated`  | `401`: the request carries no bearer token, or one that the platform does not accept. |
| `auth_unavailable` | `502`: the token could not be validated because the platform did not give a usable answer. Retrying later is the right response. |
| `not_found`        | `404`: no build with this ID belongs to the caller's tenant. The build of another tenant is indistinguishable from a build that does not exist. |
| `conflict`         | `409`: the build is still waiting or running, so its record cannot be deleted yet; cancel it first. Or the build does not wait for a session, already has one, or another user started it. Or the `builder` of the request conflicts with the existing builder of that name. |
| `too_many_builds`  | `429`: the caller's tenant already has as many builds running or waiting as it may. Submit the build again once one of them has finished. |
| `internal`         | `500`: the service could not handle the request, through no fault of the request; the details are in the service's log. `503` while the service is shutting down. Retrying later is the right response. |
| `failed`           | The build itself failed: no session attached in time, a source could not be fetched, a Kraftfile read from a source did not parse, a build step exited non-zero, the push was refused, the volume of an output does not exist or refused the import. The message is the error buildkit or the pipeline reported. |
| `cancelled`        | The build was cancelled by a request to the cancel endpoint. |
| `interrupted`      | The service restarted while the build was running, so the build was lost. It can be submitted again. |
| `builder_quota`    | The builder of the build, or the instance that imports it into a volume, could not be created or started because the tenant is over its quota. Free resources or raise the quota, then submit the build again. |

Kraftfile.description:
The Kraftfile of a build, in one of three forms: the whole file as a string,
a source to read it from, or the parsed file as an object. A source has
`session`, `git` or `url`, and none is a Kraftfile key, so the two object
forms never collide. Relative paths in the Kraftfile resolve inside the
build context.

KraftfileInline.description:
A whole Kraftfile, in YAML, as a string. The service parses it, so the
client does not need a Kraftfile parser of its own.

KraftfileObject.description:
An already-parsed Kraftfile, as an object in the JSON form of
`unikraft.com/x/kraftfile`: the same keys as the YAML file (`runtime`,
`rootfs`, `roms`, `cmd`, `env`, `labels`, ...), with `spec` optional. See
https://unikraft.com/docs/cli/reference/kraftfile for the keys. None of
`session`, `git` and `url` is one of them, which is what tells the object
apart from a source.

ListBuildsResponse.description: The response message for listing the builds of the caller's tenant.

character.description: The character within the line, counted from zero.

Position.description: A position in a source file.

name.description: The name the group is rendered under.

weak.description: Whether the group only exists while its vertices are running.

ProgressGroup.description: A group of vertices that progress renderers fold into one line.

Range.description: A range of a source file.

username.description: The username to log in with.

password.description: The password to log in with, which is never stored.

session.description:
Must be `true`: the client's session answers for the registry. For the
registry of Unikraft Cloud, the caller's token answers when the session
has no credentials.

Registry.description:
The credentials for a registry: exactly one of a `username` and `password`,
or `session` to ask the client's session for them.

session.description: The ID the client's session serves the agent under.

SSHAgent.description:
An SSH agent the build can mount with `RUN --mount=type=ssh,id=<key>`, which
only the client's session can serve.

value.description: The value of the secret, at most 500 KiB, which is never stored.

session.description: The ID the client's session serves the secret under.

Secret.description:
A secret the build can mount with `RUN --mount=type=secret,id=<key>`: exactly
one of a value in the request or a secret the client's session serves.

session.description:
The name the client's buildkit session serves the directory under.
Mutually exclusive with `git` and `url`. The build reads only the files
it needs, and a `.dockerignore` applies only when the whole `context`
directory is the build context. With `session`, a `subdir` or `filename`
cannot start with `!` or contain `*`, `?`, `[` or a backslash.

git.description:
The HTTPS URL of a git repository, cloned anonymously. Mutually exclusive
with `session` and `url`.

url.description:
The HTTPS URL of a tarball, which is fetched and unpacked. Mutually
exclusive with `session` and `git`.

ref.description:
The branch, tag or commit of a git repository to check out. Defaults to
the default branch of the repository. Only valid with `git`.

subdir.description:
A directory inside the source; the source is that directory rather than
the whole tree. Defaults to the root.

filename.description:
The file to read out of the source, relative to `subdir`. Only valid where
the source names a single file: `kraftfile`, where it defaults to
`Kraftfile`, and `contexts.dockerfile`, where it defaults to the name of
the Dockerfile the Kraftfile builds with. A `filename` on any other
context is a `400`.

Source.description:
Where the files of a build come from. A source is exactly one of a
directory the client's buildkit session serves, named by `session`, a git
repository, named by `git`, or an https tarball, named by `url`; `ref`
qualifies a repository, and `subdir` and `filename` qualify any. A git or
https source is fetched by the builder itself, not by the service, so it is
cached on the builder like any other build step. A session source is read
from the client as the build needs it, so the build waits for the session.

data.description: The contents of the file, base64-encoded.

definition.description: The LLB definition the file was lowered to.

language.description: The language of the file, e.g. `dockerfile`.

SourceInfo.description: A source file a warning points into.

inputs.description: The digests of the vertices this one depends on.

name.description: The name of the step, e.g. `[rootfs 2/4] RUN npm ci`.

cached.description: Whether the step was served from the builder's cache.

error.description: The error of the step, when it failed.

progressGroup.description: The group of steps this one is rendered as part of.

Vertex.description:
A step of the build, which buildkit calls a vertex: a pull, a Dockerfile
instruction, the packing of the image, the push, ... A vertex is reported
when it starts and again when it completes, and is identified by its digest.

vertex.description: The digest of the vertex that produced the output.

stream.description: The stream the output was written to: `1` is stdout, `2` is stderr.

timestamp.description: The time the output was produced.

VertexLog.description: A chunk of the output of a vertex.

id.description: The identifier of the status within its vertex.

vertex.description: The digest of the vertex this status belongs to.

name.description: The name of what is progressing.

total.description: The total amount of work, when known.

current.description: The amount of work done so far.

timestamp.description: The time this status was reported.

VertexStatus.description: The progress of a long-running part of a vertex, such as a download.

vertex.description: The digest of the vertex the warning belongs to.

short.description: The one-line summary of the warning, base64-encoded.

detail.description: The lines of the full explanation of the warning, base64-encoded.

sourceInfo.description: The source file the warning points into.

range.description: The ranges of the source file the warning points at.

VertexWarning.description: A warning buildkit raised while building a vertex.
